title: POLICY & PROCEDURE FOR VULNERABLE PATIENTS
html:
• PURPOSE:

To define policies guiding the care of vulnerable patients

  • SCOPE:

The entire scope of services provided to elderly, children, physically and / or mentally Challenged patients in the hospital.

  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Management
    • Medical staff
    • Nursing staff
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • COP: Care Of Patients
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
  • DEFINITION:

Vulnerable Patient:

Those patients who are prone to injury and disease by virtue of their age, sex, physical, mental and immunological status, e.g. infants, elderly, physically and mentally challenged comatose, patients under sedation, those on immunosuppressive and / or chemotherapeutic agents.

  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: NABH Standards for Hospitals.
  • POLICY:
    • Our Protocol:
      • The hospital shall offer special care taken as per the following laws and Acts to elderly patients, mentally and physically challenged people who are considered as vulnerable group.
        • Persons with disabilities (equal opportunities, protection of rights and full participation) Act, 1995.
        • Mental health Act, 1997.
        • Guardians and wards Act, 1890.
        • Consumer protection Act, 1986.
        • Protection of Human rights act.
        • Indian Penal code act
      • The vulnerable patients shall be kept in safe and secured environment to reduce the risk of abuse. Informed consent shall be obtained from patient attendee / relative if required as per policy.
      • Staff shall be trained to care for vulnerable group and awareness about vulnerable group shall be provided to all care providers.
    • Following categories of patients are referred as vulnerable at Hospital:
      • A child below 12 years of age
      • All patients aged 65 years and above
      • Terminally ill
      • Patients with intense or chronic pain
      • Patients with emotional & psychiatric disorders
      • Patients with suspected drug & / or alcohol dependency
      • Patients on ventilator support
      • Victims of abuse & neglect
      • Patients on dialysis
      • Patients on restraint
      • Patients with infectious & communicable diseases
      • Patients whose immune systems are compromised
      • Patients receiving chemo / radiotherapy
      • Patients with language barrier
      • Known allergy to food / drug / blood transfusion
    • For providing care to the vulnerable patients:

The hospital has provided a safe and secured environment of such group including:

      • Provisions of beds with padded side rails and wheels in all Intensive care unit and in few wards beds.
      • All vulnerable patients shall be received and treated in those wards where the facility is available.
      • Ramps in the premises with railing for the disabled.
      • Calling bells placed within the hand distance of the patient,
      • Frequent visit from the nursing staff.
      • Wheel chair accessibility is possible within the hospital.
      • The hospital doesn't encourage the admission falling in the above categories, without an attendant.
      • Only in case of an emergency the hospital provides immediate medical treatment and refers to appropriate authority and the liaison officer try to locate his / her family member or responsible attendant. And the case is informed to police. The mentally challenged are not admitted in the hospital, if their legal guardian does not accompany them.
    • Identifier:

Patients are identified by orange colored identification band on wrist.

  • PROCEDURE:
    • Identification of vulnerable patients:
      • For identified “At Risk” Category, use an Orange colored identification wrist band & list them under “Vulnerable” patients.
    • Use of Restraints / Posey Belts for Confused Patient:
      • Ensure the use of restraints on patient if need arises (e.g. hand / Posey belt) and document the action plan into the Nursing Care plan
      • Ensure that patient and relatives are informed of the reason for the use of restraints i.e. to safeguard the confused patient form failing.
      • Patient’s restraints should be checked on every shift and documented into the activity flow sheet / Nursing care Plan
      • If the need arises then a sitting companion should be requested for the patient
      • Nursing Activity Flow sheet on every shift should be reviewed to ensure proper care has been rendered
      • Besides reviewing for fall risk on every shift, reassessment of the patient should be done when there is a change from current status.
      • Immediate and Post Op Patients within the next 48 hours
      • Patients transferred from Intensive Care / Operating Theatre
      • Post-fall patient
      • Actions taken should be entered into the Nursing Activity Flow sheet and HIS
    • Prevention of patient fall:
      • Care for Children:

Incidence of childhood falls is highest in infancy and declines throughout childhood

        • Young children should be supervised at all times and kept off high surfaces to prevent fall injuries.
        • Gates on stairways effectively prevent falls. Light, collapsible gates are readily available.
        • Fall from cribs can occur when the infants begin to stand and climb. The mattress level should be adjusted at an age-appropriate time.
        • The most effective tool for preventing fall from windows is a window guard.
        • Safety devices for children to prevent unintentional falls include grab bars in the tub or shower or next to the toilet and nonskid mats in the tub or shower. Floors should be kept free of clutter and other tripping hazards.
        • When children are ready to sleep in a regular bed, side rails should be used to avoid falls.
        • Patient should be assigned to a bed that enables him / her to exit toward his / her stronger side whenever possible.
        • The patient's coordination and balance should be assessed before assisting with transfer and mobility activities.
        • Implementation of bowel and bladder program should be done to decrease urgency and incontinence.
        • All staff should:
        • Approach patient towards unaffected side to maximize participation in care.
        • Transfer patient towards stronger side.
        • Education of patient and attendant should be done for
        • All aspects of Fall Prevention Program.
        • All activities prior to initiating assistive devices.
        • Usage of grab bars.
        • Medication time / dose, side effects, and interactions with food / medications.
        • Equipments should be:
        • Locked (movable equipment) before transferring patients.
        • Individualized according to patient needs.
        • Environment:
        • Placing patient care articles within reach.
        • Providing physically safe environment (eliminating spills, clutter, electrical cords, and unnecessary equipment)
        • Providing adequate lighting.
        • Medical staff should:
        • Evaluate and treat gait changes, postural instability and spasticity.
        • Initiate treatment for impaired vision, hearing.
        • Evaluate medication profile for fall risk.
        • Evaluate and treat pain.
        • Evaluate and treat orthostatic hypotension.
        • Assess and treat impaired central processing (dementia, delirium, stroke, perception)
      • Care of Adults:
        • Every patient admitted to the hospital is to be assessed for “fall risk” as part of the admission process.
        • The actions and responsibilities of the nurses in the assessment to prevent falls for the hospitalized patients should be defined.
        • If the patient is found to be at-risk for falls, then following measures should be taken
        • Explain / educate patient and/or relative on safety precautions/awareness on fall prevention
        • Enter the name of patient or relative into the Nursing Assessment form.
        • Assign patient to a room / bed near the nurses’ station where possible, for better observation.
        • Ensure that the bedside locker an overhead table is within easy reach of patient.
        • Ensure all the bed rails are up at all times when patient is in bed. Enter into the Nursing care plan if patient or relative refuses to have bed rails up
        • Ensure bed castors are locked in position at all times.
        • Ensure that call bell is within reach of patient and in good working condition. Demonstrate to patient or relative on how to use the call bell.
        • Offer bedpan/urinal to patient or assist patient to the toilet before giving sedation. Reinforce with the use of call bell.
        • Check patient on regular intervals or when necessary to attend as per patient needs (e.g. toileting). Enter any special care plan/interventions into the Nursing Care plan
        • Mention any action taken, into Nursing activity Flow sheet and NCP and handover to next shift.
        • Ensure that information on vulnerable patient is passed to the next shift during the nurses’ report.
        • Proper analysis of all potential fall risk cases at ward level by senior nurse is essential. Identify possible solutions and share with the ward staff.
        • If still after preventive measures a fall occurs :
        • Charge Nurse should be notified immediately
        • The Resident Medical Officer should be immediately notified and a complete patient assessment should be done which should be entered into the patient medical record
        • Each ward must document the number of falls per month.
        • The number of falls per month area wise should be monitored by Nursing QA as well.
    • Comments:
      • Prompt attention and service shall be provided while minimizing waiting times in OPD & diagnostics for vulnerable patients.
      • Elderly patients who are having difficulty in walking or are bedridden must be identified and all help should be ensured to them to see the doctor or get admitted to the ward.
      • Ward boys shall be alerted by the staff comes across such patients first and arrangements shall be made for conveyance in a wheel chair.
      • Physically challenged patients should be provided with a wheel chair or trolley to go about in the hospital to avail its various facilities.
      • All such IPD patients, other than in ICU shall be screened for special assistance needs during hospitalization.
      • All Nursing Assessment on admission or reassessment of patients during any phase of stay depending on progress of the patient shall be carried out to identify any changing needs.
      • Depending on the vulnerable aspect, each patient will be provided with actions and support to ensure that care and safety aspects are addressed.
      • Vulnerable patients will not be left alone at any given time.
      • A female attendant shall attend female patients and children of both genders for their physical interventions such as bathing and toilet.
      • All minors shall be admitted along with an attendant approved by the family
      • Any special requests made by the patient/family will be respected.
      • A list of vulnerable patients is generated in the daily census and informed to the Nursing superintendent.
      • Regular monitoring will be ensured by supervisory staff to ensure the safety and security of vulnerable patients.
      • Side rails on bed shall be provided to vulnerable patients to ensure safety.
      • There shall be one responsible bystander always with the patient.
      • Relatives shall be explained about patient condition and educated about diet and health activities.
      • Counseling facility for mentally challenged patients shall be provided.
      • Physiotherapy facilities for mentally and physically challenged patients shall be provided.
      • Mentally challenged patients shall be given special attention by a nurse.
      • The nursing staff and the attendees shall show maximum tolerance and patience while dealing with these patients.
      • Attendants / relatives shall be encouraged to be with them whenever advisable.
      • Special care should be taken by the treating doctor or the attending nurse/technician to explain things related to the disease and treatment carefully and patiently.
      • In case informed consent needs to be obtained while treating a child or mentally challenged patient, it shall be ensured that consent is obtained from the persons directly related to the patient like father, mother, brothers or sisters.
      • Everything about the proposed procedure / treatments shall be informed along with possibilities of likely complications that may arise.
      • Signature of the patient or immediate relatives shall be obtained along with time and date.
